name: Data.auxLift_injective_and_hasSum_inner
summary: The Rallis inner product formula for the edge of the auxiliary pair gives one constant C ≠ 0 for every twist; the adjoint lift is (the algebraic form of) the theta lift by the sharp datum F ⊗ vac, F = γ·levelIndicator, and the coset sum gives the formula with gramFactor.

steps.claim: The Rallis inner product formula by doubling (`rallis_inner_product_euler`) for the edge of the auxiliary pair auxPair(D, 1, j) of the trivial twist (`Data.fitsParams_auxPair`, `AuxPair.FitsParams.isEdge`), on S = W_j, the rank condition 2·rk W_j < rk V_j holding: there is C ≠ 0 such that for all characters a, b of the weights of the edge and every sharp finite datum F of level J and constant c, the lift L of forms of level J by v ⊗ F satisfies L y = 0 → y = 0 and ⟨L y′, L y⟩ = ∑_γ C·c·cosetTerm(…). The real data, hence C, do not depend on the twist.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨C, hC, H⟩ := rallis_inner_product_euler (S :=
    D.spaceW j) (D.fitsParams_auxPair .one j).isEdge (by grind [card_rowIndex, card_V])

steps.claim: Take A = C·#WeylIndex(Y(D, 1), κ(auxPair(D, 1, j))), a product of non-zero numbers; let ϑ be a tame character.
steps.lean: use C * card (WeylIndex (D.Y 1) (D.auxPair .one j).κ), mul_ne_zero hC NeZero.out, fun ϑ ↦ ?_

steps.claim: Write O for the auxiliary pair auxPair(D, ϑ, j).

The datum of O gives an arrow A′ from W_j to V_j (`IsEdge.isArrow`); and F = #TwistGL(O, r)·levelIndicator(O) has the support property f and the norm c: ∑|F|² = #TwistGL(O, r)²·(∏_{w∈Q} q_w)^{(n−r)·r} (`AuxPair.levelIndicator_support_and_normSq`).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨A, f, c⟩ := ((D.fitsParams_auxPair ..).isEdge.isArrow O.a O.b O.auxDatum.2).1,
    O.levelIndicator_support_and_normSq

steps.claim: For every y of principal level on W_j, auxLift(D, ϑ, j)(y) is the algebraic form of the theta lift of y by the datum with real part v_{P_ξ} (ξ the highest vector) and finite part modDatum(F): by adjointness (`Data.inner_auxLift`) and `AuxPair.adjoint_theta_eq_formLift`, it is the algebraic form of the lift by v ⊗ Υ, which equals the lift by modDatum(F, v) because y has principal level (`AuxPair.lift_auxDatum_eq_lift_modDatum`, `IsArrow.eq_formLift_of_coe_eq`).
steps.lean:
have U y := (congrArg _ (O.adjoint_theta_eq_formLift (D.fitsParams_auxPair ϑ j)
    (D.inner_auxLift ϑ y))).trans ((ofAlgForm_toAlgForm
    ..).trans (congrArg _ (A.eq_formLift_of_coe_eq _ (A.coe_formLift _ ▸
    O.lift_auxDatum_eq_lift_modDatum _ (A y.1).1 (mem_levelSpace_formRep_iff.1 y.2)))))

steps.claim: Apply step 1 to the characters a(O), b(O) and the datum F ⊗ vac, which is sharp for the principal level at the places of 𝔪 and their conjugates (`isSharp_modDatum`: 𝔪 has places (`Data.nonempty_modulus_places`), the tame part of b(O) is 1 off them, F has the support property and ∑|F|² ≠ 0), and to every y of principal level, whose level contains the one required (`LevelPlaces.ker_reductionK₀_eq`): its lift L y vanishes only for y = 0, and ⟨L x, L y⟩ = ∑_γ C·c₀·cosetTerm(…) with c₀ = ∑|F|²/#(matrices mod 𝔪)/#GL_r(O_E/𝔪).
steps.lean:
replace H (y : D.principalForms _) := H O.a O.b (isSharp_modDatum (stdSpace ..) _
    (.inr (by apply nonempty_modulus_places)) _ f (O.tame_eq_one · <|
    places_levelModulus.ge.mt ·) (by simp [↓c, prod_eq_zero_iff])) _ (mem_levelSpace_formRep_iff.1
    y.2 · ∘ by simp [O.ker_reductionK₀_eq, levelOf, funext_iff]; tauto)

steps.claim: Injectivity: if auxLift(D, ϑ, j)(y) = 0 then the lift L y is 0 by step 5, so y = 0 by step 6. There remains the sum formula, for all x, y.
steps.lean: use .of_ker _ fun y z ↦ Subtype.ext ((H y).1 (Subtype.ext (U y ▸ z ▸ map_zero _))), fun x y ↦ ?_

steps.claim: The inner product of the algebraic forms auxLift(D, ϑ, j)(x), auxLift(D, ϑ, j)(y) is [K₀ : level]·#WeylIndex times the Petersson product of the corresponding forms (`LevelPlaces.LevelForm.inner_eq_petersson`), which by step 5 are the lifts L x, L y.

Multiplying the series of step 6 by this factor gives, term by term, A·gramFactor(O)·rallisTerm(D, ϑ, j, spaceW(D, j), x, y, γ), by the definition of gramFactor(O) and the value of ∑|F|² (step 4); a ring identity.
steps.lean: exact (((H y).2 _).mul_left _).congr_fun fun _ ↦ by push_cast [gramFactor, c]; ring!
